title: presubmit: add batched presubmit validator with dependency quarantine
author: Maya Rivera
description: Motivation: presubmit runtimes have grown linearly with repo size and noisy dependency updates cause frequent churn and flakiness. This PR introduces a lightweight presubmit 'shepherd' that batches small changes into a single validation run, and a dependency quarantine mechanism that automatically isolates suspicious transitive updates for manual review. Summary: - Add a batched presubmit workflow (GH actions-based) that groups related commits in the same push into one validation run (saves CI tokens and reduces queue pressure). - Introduce tools/dep-quarantine to detect semver-skew and newly-introduced transitive dependencies, and mark them as quarantined in the presubmit context so tests run against a guarded environment. - Add a minimal Python-based presubmit shepherd service (scripts/presubmit_shepherd.py) that coordinates event aggregation for a short window (30s by default) and triggers a single CI job per batch. - Add documentation and runbook at docs/ci/presubmit-batching.md and docs/ci/dep-quarantine-runbook.md - Add a small set of unit and integration tests for the shepherd and quarantine detectors. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-4512) - [x] Tests added (unit + integration smoke) - [x] CI config updated - [x] Runbook and oncall playbook added - [x] Backwards compatible default behavior (batch window defaults to 0 in local dev) Why this matters: large teams were repeatedly spinning up duplicate CI runs for trivial commits which increased queue latency and CI cost. The quarantine ensures we don't silently accept risky transitive changes into release branches. Backwards compatibility & rollout: This is feature-flagged via a repo-level config (infra/ci/presubmit-config.yaml). New behaviour is off for the first 48 hours post-merge (automated toggle) to monitor telemetry. Related: ENG-4630 (dep curation initiative), SUP-2103 (customer-reported flaky presubmit). Migration notes: - Small ops change: add a webhook-secret entry to prod secrets store for the shepherd service. - Ops should monitor CI queue length and quarantine alerts for 72 hours after rollout. Rollout plan included in docs/ci/presubmit-batching.md.

review_comments: Ola Henriksen: Nice direction — can you be explicit about how this interacts with branch-protection enforced status checks? We need to ensure quarantined PRs still block merges until manual review.

Maya Rivera: The presubmit shepherd marks quarantined PRs with a required status 'quarantine/manual-review' and we added steps in the GH workflow to fail that check. Branch protection mapping documented in docs/ci/dep-quarantine-runbook.md.
Priya Nair: The batched workflow looks good but CI cache keys might collide when multiple language stacks are involved. Suggest namespacing the cache by repo path + batch id.
Maya Rivera: Updated infra/ci/cache-config.yaml to include batch id and language tag, and added a test that simulates concurrent batches to assert no cache pollution.
Devon Clarke: We saw one flaky test in the detector integration on first run — looks like a time-dependent golden file. Please make it tolerant to timestamp differences or freeze time in the test.
Maya Rivera: Fixed the test to use a deterministic timestamp and added a small tolerance window. Reran integration tests locally and on CI.
